newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government is considering a compromise on car industry assistance where tariffs would be gradually cut from 15 per cent in 2000 to 10 per cent in 2005. In addition to this, the Export Facilitation Scheme would be replaced by another form of industry assistance, possibly a production bounty, and extra funds would be provided for research and development. Page 1

Major credit card companies Visa and MasterCard yesterday launched the world's first "virtual" credit card for use on the Internet. The product, a Visa or Mastercard icon that sits on a personal computer screen in an electronic purse and ensures payment or products over the Internet, will be in Australia in under two months. Page 1.

David Jones Ltd's new managing director, Peter Wilkinson, acknowledges he has a difficult task in restoring the company's credibility. Wilkinson plans to introduce reforms to improve efficiency, such as targeting customer service levels for improved performance and reviewing the long-standing competitive pricing policy. Page 23.

The planned November public float of Telstra is proceeding according to plan thereby limiting the window of opportunity for Optus Communications to launch its sharemarket listing before Christmas. The Telstra public float continues to be strongly advocated by the Federal Government, especially in light of Telstra's attempts to rewrite its pay-TV contract with News Ltd. Page 24.

Junior gold company Mineral Commodities NL has confirmed a major gold discovery near its White Foil prospect at Kalgoorlie. The find comes after a year of exploration with its venture partner, the French group Cogema. Findings indicate a major new gold system only 20 kilometres from Kalgoorlie. Page 27.

Centennial Coal Company Ltd yesterday confirmed it will outlay A$5.5 million to obtain a controlling stake in the Cook colliery. The move signals the company's entry into the Queensland coking coal, and coal fields industry. Centennial will also join Cook's other major owner, Glencorp International, in outlaying A$3 million in the first year of operation to improving the productivity of the mine. Page 27.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australis Media has stated that it believes a full merger with Optus Vision is the most effective way to circumvent last week's Supreme Court ruling which disallowed a proposed infrastructure sharing arrangement between the two pay TV companies. Page 21.

Bankers Trust International yesterday removed the managers of the A$90 million Rural Property Trust, thereby ending a long-standing conflict over the Trust's performance, and enabling the organisation to be corporatised under new management. The former managers, Rural & Agricultural Management, accepted A$500,000 in compensation for their loss of managerial power. Page 21.

Pharmaceutical giant FH Faulding plans to expand into the prosperous US health care market through a A$90 million takeover of its North American subsidiary, Faulding Inc. FH Faulding announced last night it would offer US$12 a share for the 38 per cent of the company it does not control. Page 21.

The plan by BHP to sell high quality direct reduced iron (DRI) to the North American steel market appears set to proceed with BHP's board expected to decide later this month in favour of the project. The plan is a A$1 billion joint venture with Venezuelan steel giant Siderurgica Venezolana Sivensa.

Senior partner in Arnold Bloch Leibler, and Coles Myer director Mark Leibler has called on the Australian Taxation Office to explain its role in the "witch-hunt atmosphere" surrounding a claim by the former Labor Government that 100 wealthy people were avoiding tax worth approximately A$800 million per year. He further commented that recent evidence has cast considerable doubt on the claim. Page 23.

A ruling by the Federal Court that fundraising activities by the New South Wales-based United Tree Farmers are illegal has raised the prospect of receivership unless the situation can be repaired within 28 days. The Australian Securities Commission filed charges against the company, and four others, over plans to raise A$6.5 million from investors for a ti-tree growing scheme in Queensland. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The NSW Opposition claims the State Government must rectify a mistake in the TAB privatisation legislation or the sale price may fall below A$1 billion. Shadow Treasurer Ron Phillips said the mistake related to the licence time limit, scheduled for accounting standards. Page 25.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday characterised the Federal Government's A$2 billion savings rebate as a "reward to thrifty Australians" however he was unable to confirm the scheme would lead to a rise in national saving. His comments came after Treasury investigations revealed the proposed A$450 maximum rebate could actually reduce national savings. Page 27.

Australian internet researcher Ramin Marzbani yesterday claimed Telstra earns at least A75 cents out of every Australian dollar spent on Internet services and is poised to increase its market share further. The rise in market share represents a 25 per cent increase from the level Telstra enjoyed two years ago. Page 27.

National Mutual managing director Geoff Tomlinson yesterday pressured the Federal Government to implement the recommendations of the Wallis inquiry, in particular the removal of prudential regulation powers from the Reserve Bank of Australia. Tomlinson warned that accountability within regulatory structures was also necessary for the efficiency of the financial system. Page 29.

Top Australian exporter Cryofab Industries could be sold to off-share interests following its decision to implement voluntary administration. Company administrator Kevin Shirlaw said Cryofab has three major secured creditors and several hundred unsecured creditors. Page 29.

BHP Petroleum has increased its commitment to frontier exploration via an agreement with Algeria's State-owned Sonatrach oil company. Under the deal, BHP will spend A$82 million over the coming decade to target various areas for oil exploration. Page 29.
THE AGE

Consultants to the Industry Commission have sharply revised their estimates of the consumer benefits of cutting car tariffs from A$3 billion to A$75 million. The move eases pressure on the Federal Government to radically slash car industry tariffs. Page B3.

The Victorian Government yesterday launched its efforts to attract foreign investment by promoting Melbourne as the most cost effective city in the region. The State Government spearheaded its launch by promoting Advantage Melbourne, an independent benchmark study that details the benefits of investing and doing business in Victoria. Page B3.

Westpac's A$1.44 billion takeover bid for the Bank of Melbourne faces a further obstruction from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, which stated yesterday that it would be seeking more information on the bid from Westpac. In particular the ACCC will be investigating the market consequences of the takeover. Page B3.

Far-reaching reform of ANZ Banking Group's finance offshoot, Esanda Finance Corp has revised the company's interim net profit downwards by 20.4 per cent to A$39 million for the six months to March 31. Esanda aims to become a non-branch operation based on mortgage originators. Page B3.

The Royal Automobile Club of Victoria has recorded after-tax profit of A$31 million for the 1996-1997 financial year. The strong performance has been credited to improved investment returns and operational reforms. Page B3.

Telstra has been disappointed with its ventures into both the telephony and Pay-TV industries as they have returned low profits. The telecommunication giant's on-line services however, have performed surprising well since their introduction in 1995. Page B4.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
